summary.prose: This Story stops the index from losing relationships and makes it say when it is incomplete. A relationship whose target is not stored yet is kept as a pending row that waits for the target's id and is completed by the cross-file pass once the target exists, including after another repository's reindex; a re-export line is stored as an EXPORTS edge plus an entry in an export-name index that the call matcher reads, so aliased re-exports resolve; and a reindex deletes everything the repository holds and builds it again from every file. Each repository gets a recorded state (IndexState) whose counts are written in the same transactions as the rows they count; its completeness is returned beside the unchanged status by the daemon's status requests, shown in the CLI and both editor plugins, and carried into every analyzer lookup that reads relationships.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Three layers, each depending only on the one below. Layer 1, the file commit: the store has one write operation for a file, which in a single LMDB transaction replaces the file's entities, replaces its relationships and its pending relationships, and advances the repository's generation and completeness counters. It grows out of the existing whole-file replacement (reindexFile), which already replaces a file's entities in one transaction but removes relationships only for entities that disappeared from the file; the commit goes further and replaces the outgoing relationships of every entity of the file. The indexer's refresh, the delete event and the repair all call it; a file is selected for it by one filter built from the repository's ignore files. A relationship is never dropped in the commit: when its target is not stored it becomes a pending row, and pending rows are completed only by the passes that own them: the cross-file pass for code symbols, and the two endpoint passes of the external-services Epic for theirs. Layer 2, the recorded state: one row per repository holds the generation and what is known to be incomplete (relationships awaiting a target that is in an indexed repository, relationships that could not be written, entities without vectors). The four repository status values keep their meaning; completeness is a separate field read from this row and shown wherever status is shown, so a repository with anything outstanding does not read as fully ready. Layer 3, derived data: evidence is a one-byte value on the relationship row, written in the commit, by the cross-file pass and by every other writer of a stored relationship; subsystem grouping, subsystem summaries and model-proposed document relationships are queued passes that start only from a repository whose state is complete, write their own tables, and stamp what they wrote with the generation it was computed from. All new stored data arrives as steps on the existing migration chain (SCHEMA_VERSION 4 onward); no existing edge key or kind byte changes.

ownedContracts.name: IndexState
ownedContracts.purpose: The recorded per-repository state: the generation of the graph and what is known to be incomplete. Written in the same transaction as every file commit and by the cross-file pass; read by repository status, by the commit's callers, and by every derived pass to decide whether it may run and whether what it wrote is stale.

boundary.internal: The rule that a relationship with an absent target becomes pending instead of being skipped, at each of the six places in src/db/relations.ts where one is lost today (the resolved write's skip on a missing endpoint and its skip on a kind with no byte, promoteToResolved, promoteResolvedBatch, and the pending write's discard of a row without its file or repository and of a row whose repository is not registered), each either kept as pending or counted as unwritable with a reason; the set of files whose parse or commit failed in a full index, persisted with their paths until they next commit; which fields of the state are recounted on open and which are persisted and carried over; the classification of a pending relationship as awaiting-target, ambiguous or no-candidate, with the external-service rows classed apart and the two endpoint passes counted in when a full index is finished; the class is stored on the pending row itself, in its existing free-form record, so no stored form changes, a row the cross-file pass has not yet attempted counts as awaiting-target, and the recount on open reads the stored class and does not run resolution again; the extension of the cross-file pass to complete relationships awaiting a target by id, for imports and the other code-symbol kinds as well as calls and inheritance, and to follow a re-exporting file to the function it re-exports; the lookup of pending rows by the id they await, with its migration step, and the pass after a file event visiting the rows that await an entity of the files just committed; the change of the reindex request so that it deletes the repository's rows in the graph store and the vector store and builds them again from every file, in place of today's skip of unchanged files, with no separate repair request, returning to pending the relationships that other repositories hold into the deleted entities, and its queuing by the migration for every repository indexed before this change, which starts as not complete; the storing of the repository entity so that the manifest step's dependency relationships are written; the measurement on this repository, before and after a repair, of the awaiting-target, ambiguous, no-candidate and unwritable counts, with unwritable expected to be zero; the IndexState row, its migration step, its recount on open, and the derivation of repository status from it, as a completeness field returned beside the unchanged status by the daemon's status and stats requests and shown in the CLI's repository pane and in both editor plugins; and the analyzer's read of it: an analyzer lookup that reads relationships of a repository that is not complete says so in its result, with the counts, so that an answer over an incomplete graph is not returned as a plain fact. The choice, in this Story's design, of the function reached only through a re-exporting file that the repair is measured on, since the issue's own example (pickScope) has been removed from the source. Raising the log level of a refused relationship from debug is internal. Until Story s2 lands, s1 applies its rule inside the existing separate writes.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The extension of the existing whole-file replacement into the file commit (relationships and pending rows in the same transaction as entities; outgoing relationships of surviving entities replaced, not only those of entities that disappeared; incoming relationships of a removed entity returned to pending), the move of the indexer's refresh and delete paths and of the clean-up pass's removal of a stored file onto it, and the retirement of the separate delete-then-upsert sequence in the indexer. The handling of vectors after the commit: writing the entity row with its embedding marker empty and setting it in a second transaction only after the vector write succeeds, counting an entity with an empty marker in IndexState, comparing entity ids with the vector table on open in both directions, so that a vector left behind by a failed removal is deleted before a plain insert can meet it, and the extension of the existing reembed job to run on daemon start and after an index, with a vector write for an entity whose marker is empty made an upsert, except for an entity first allocated in the same commit, which keeps the plain insert. Three things in that job change with it: it applies the embed step's own selection instead of forcing every entity, so empty-body entities (external endpoints, module stubs) stay unselected and uncounted; its update of an embedding writes the vector first and sets the marker in a second transaction, where today it sets the marker first; and the marker carries the model of the backend that is active, not one fixed name. Which entities count as unembedded (those the embed step selects) and the separate recorded reason when the embedding backend is unavailable. The count of a file whose commit fails on a file event. The queue rule that index jobs go ahead of other jobs and that a long job yields between its units, so that a commit is not held behind a model pass. How a reader sees the old or the new set during a commit is the store's ordinary transaction isolation and needs no new mechanism.

The by-file and by-repository index of entity rows, its migration step that builds it for an existing store, and its upkeep. No single entity-row write exists today: there are seven raw put and remove sites across src/db/entities.ts and src/db/graph/migrations.ts, and the existing name index is kept in step by a helper each site must remember to call. This Story introduces one put and one remove function for entity rows that maintain the name index and the new index together, routes every raw site through them, and adds a test that fails when a raw put or remove appears outside them. Upkeep therefore sits beneath every caller, so that neither today's writers nor the file commit need to know of it and this Story does not depend on s2. The two reads (findEntitiesByFile, listEntitiesForRepo) keep their results and their callers; a new existence check answers whether a repository holds any entity, and the analyzer's scope check uses it.

The cause, which ISSUE-0d577569 records as not known, was reproduced on 2026-10-11 and is not the system's semaphore limit, which the library's message names, but the loss of the daemon's own file lock on the store's lock file, after which another process that opens and closes the store removes the store's semaphores; the daemon's next write then fails with the library's message about the limit, and its exit hangs in the library's close. What in the daemon closes a second descriptor on the lock file is not yet identified. First, therefore, the remedy that does not depend on finding it: the live store is opened by the daemon alone, and any other process is refused it. Second, a bound on the whole shutdown including the store's close, so that a close that hangs ends in an exit. Third, recording a store failure of this kind and stating it in the daemon's status. None of this is consumed by another Story.

The refusal, with a named error and its own code, of a search or analyze request about a repository whose status is indexing, at the analyzer's scope check and at the daemon's search requests, carrying the status and how far the run has got (files done of files selected, and when it began), read from the indexer's running job; the tools that rest on the analyzer (the workflow steps, triage, code review) pass that error on as it is. The order of the analyzer's run: the refusal of a scope the index does not hold comes before a size is announced, or the announcement says the size could not be counted. The named cause and error code for a failed read of the last-indexed time and for a failed lookup, and the three other defects of ISSUE-e2bcadd9 (the wrong provider named, the scope resolved before the cache, and failure text matched inside echoed output). This Story does not read IndexState: it works with the checks the analyzer has today, so that it stays independent of s1.

nonFunctional.performance: Reading one file's entities costs in proportion to that file's rows, and one repository's in proportion to that repository's rows. A file commit is one write transaction whose size is bounded by one file. A first full index holds more pending rows than today until the cross-file pass runs, and that pass does more work; this is accepted under the accuracy rule. Index jobs take precedence in the queue and a derived pass yields between its units of work, so a commit waits for at most one unit of a pass. Model calls are serial; the mid-tier pass sends only new or changed documents. Vector writes keep the plain insert for entities first stored in the same commit, so a first full index writes vectors at today's cost; the upsert, which costs more against a large vector table, is used only for changed entities and for the backfill, and Story s2's design measures it on this repository.
nonFunctional.security: No store is opened outside the daemon and no model is reached except through the local provider or the CLI providers. The ignore-file proposal sends the model file names and manifest names, not file contents, and writes into the user's repository only when no root ignore file exists. Document text sent to the mid-tier model goes through the user's own CLI session, as other mid-tier calls do.
nonFunctional.observability: Repository status carries the completeness counts and the reason a repository is incomplete. A relationship the store refuses is logged at warn with its reason and counted, not logged at debug. A fallback ignore file, a skipped language reader, a store failure after its locks were taken away, and a model-proposed capability that is off each state their cause where status is read. Each derived row carries the generation it was computed from.
nonFunctional.durability: The file commit is atomic in LMDB: after a crash a file holds its old rows or its new rows. Vectors are written after the commit and may be missing after a crash; the gap is recorded by an empty embedding marker, checked against the vector table on open, and backfilled, and the repository reads as incomplete until it is, unless the embedding backend is unavailable, which is reported as its own reason. The IndexState fields that the tables can answer are recounted when the store is opened; the rest, including the paths of files that could not be committed, are persisted in the state row and survive a restart. Every new table and value arrives by a migration step applied on open; no existing key or kind byte changes, so an older store is brought forward without a re-index. Derived tables can be dropped and recomputed without loss.

api.name: runCrossFileResolver

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: As today (db, repoRoot, sourceRoots, scopeFile?), plus mode: 'full' | 'settle' | 'repository' (explicit; default 'repository') and committedFiles?: readonly string[] (required in 'settle' mode: the files committed since the last settle).

returns.meaning: As today, plus completedById (rows promoted because their awaited target now exists) and pendingByClass (the repository's counts after the pass).

errors.condition: A store failure, propagated as today (it fails a full index).

postconditions: Pass 0 (new): promotes code-symbol rows whose awaited target is now stored, read through unresolved_by_target: in 'settle' mode, the rows awaiting an entity of committedFiles; in 'full' mode, the rows awaiting ANY entity of the repository, whichever repository holds them (a guard: no indexed kind crosses workspace repositories today, Pass 2 being single-repository, so this restores only an edge written by hand or by a future cross-repository kind); in 'repository' mode, the repository's own awaiting rows. Counts move in each owning repository's index_state row.

Classification of a row awaiting a FILE entity id whose file is not stored, in 'full' mode after the walk and in 'settle' mode for the rows the committed files wrote, by the full index's own file-selection rule (index.ts:630-640: the repository's ignore list, a parser for the extension, not generated or minified) plus the artifact parser's skip rules (SKIP_BASENAMES and MAX_SIZE, artifact.ts:89, :117-118), extracted so the full index and the cross-file pass apply one rule: (1) the file does not pass the rule as code (no parser for its extension, generated or minified, a SKIP_BASENAMES lock file, over MAX_SIZE): class 'no-candidate', meta.reason 'target-not-code', not counted against graphComplete; (2) a parser handles it but the ignore rule excludes it: stays 'awaiting-target' with meta.reason 'target-excluded-by-ignore', counted against graphComplete and named in the reasons; (3) it passes the rule but is not stored (its parse or write failed): stays 'awaiting-target' with meta.reason 'target-not-committed', and the file is in uncommittedFiles. Story s6 replaces the ignore-list part of the rule with its filter; this Story only extracts and reuses the rule the full index applies today.
Pass 1 rewires module-stub imports as today.

Pass 1's import rewire writes carry meta.repo = repoRoot and meta.file = the importing file's absolute path (today they carry no meta, src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:242-244), so a rewire kept awaiting is found by the file's deletes.

Pass 1b (new): pending EXPORTS rows are resolved to the named exported entity of the file their specifier resolves to (or that file entity for rawTo '*'), promoted to EXPORTS edges with today's empty value, and in the same transaction an export_names entry (re-exporting file id, exported name) -> target id is written ('*' rows under the name '*').

Pass 2 attempts every code-symbol kind it can resolve by name (CALLS, INHERITS, IMPLEMENTS, REFERENCES) and leaves boundary kinds to the endpoint passes; resolveCall widens a caller's candidates by looking up the call's raw name in export_names of each imported file and following '*' entries to their source files, transitively with a visited set, so an aliased re-export resolves by its exported name. An export_names entry whose target id is not stored is ignored.

Every row Pass 2 attempts has meta.class written in EVERY mode ('full', 'settle', 'repository'): 'ambiguous' (with candidates) when several match, and 'no-candidate' (reason 'no-match') when its intent is UNRESOLVED, which is the common case of a call to a builtin or a library function; only rows awaiting an id stay 'awaiting-target'. So an edit that adds an unresolvable call leaves a complete repository complete. In 'full' mode, after Pass 2, every code-symbol row with no class and no awaitsId that Pass 2 does not attempt (any unresolved IMPORTS) is written 'no-candidate' as well. Counts and generation are written in the same transactions as the promotions and reclassifications.

api.name: fullIndex

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The repository to index from scratch.

returns.meaning: The repository's rows in both stores are rebuilt from every file.

errors.condition: A cross-file pass or store failure, as today: status 'error', lastRun 'failed'.

postconditions: Before the walk: every relationship another repository holds into this repository's entities is written back as a pending row of the holding repository awaiting the entity's id (a guard: the indexer writes no such edge today); then deleteEntitiesForRepo and deleteUnresolvedForRepo remove the repository's rows in the graph store and the vector store, with its export_names entries; IndexState is reset (generation kept and advanced, counts zeroed, fullIndexFinished false). The cross-file pass runs with mode 'full'.

The delete also removes, as deleteEntitiesForRepo does today, the repository's document summaries and its cached exploration outputs: the cache describes the old graph and must go; the summaries are regenerated from current content by the doc-summarise-repo job the full index queues at its end, with model calls (the summary tier). No other stored data of the repository survives a reindex.

The selection loop's rule is extracted into one predicate that the cross-file pass also calls, so a file is 'outside the graph by design', 'excluded by the ignore rule' or 'selected' by the same test in both places.
Every selected file is parsed and written (indexFile with cleanFirst semantics: no unchanged-hash skip).

A selected file that is not stored is added to IndexState.uncommittedFiles with its path, whether its parse or write throws or indexFile returns false without throwing (its read failed: the file vanished or is unreadable; a full index makes no unchanged-hash skip, and a selected file always has a parser, so a false return always means not stored); a file that writes is removed from it.
The manifest step's DEPENDS_ON writes carry meta.repo, so a refused one is counted against this repository.
The repository entity (kind 'repo') is stored before the manifest step, so its DEPENDS_ON edges are written.
After the cross-file pass and both endpoint passes, fullIndexFinished is set true and endpointPassFailed records whether either endpoint pass threw.

errorCases.scenario: A file's parse or write throws during a full index.
errorCases.detection: The per-file try/catch in the full-index loop catches the error.
errorCases.response: The file's path is added to IndexState.uncommittedFiles (and removed when a later write of it succeeds); the full index continues with the next file as today.
errorCases.userImpact: Completeness lists '1 file could not be indexed' with the path; analyzer lookups that read relationships say completeness is not established.

errorCases.scenario: A selected file cannot be read during a full index (it vanished between listing and read, or is unreadable).
errorCases.detection: indexFile returns false from its read catch (src/indexer/index.ts:1027-1029); the full-index loop sees the false return (today it only counts it as skipped, :655-656).
errorCases.response: The path is added to IndexState.uncommittedFiles like a file whose parse throws; rows awaiting its file id stay 'awaiting-target' with reason 'target-not-committed'.
errorCases.userImpact: Completeness lists the file as not indexed; a reindex or the file's next event retries it.

errorCases.scenario: The external-endpoint or messaging-endpoint pass throws at the end of a full index.
errorCases.detection: The existing try/catch around each endpoint pass in fullIndex.
errorCases.response: IndexState.endpointPassFailed is set true and fullIndexFinished set true; the repository's status follows today's rule. graphComplete is therefore false.
errorCases.userImpact: The repository reads not complete with reason 'the endpoint pass failed'; a reindex retries it.

errorCases.scenario: The cross-file pass fails part-way (store error in a promotion transaction).
errorCases.detection: The error propagates out of runCrossFileResolver into fullIndex, as today.
errorCases.response: Status 'error' and lastRun 'failed' as today; fullIndexFinished stays false because it is written only after the pass and both endpoint passes end. Promotions already committed keep their IndexState updates, since each was written in its own transaction with its count.
errorCases.userImpact: The repository reads under index ('error') and not complete; the analyzer refuses it with 'repo-indexing' (not retryable) as s5 defined.

errorCases.scenario: A write transaction that changes pending rows or counts unwritables aborts (store error, or the daemon stops mid-transaction).
errorCases.detection: withWriteTxn rejects, or on the next open the recount from the stored classes is compared with the index_state row's pending counts.
errorCases.response: The rows and the counts were written in the same LMDB transaction, so both are rolled back together and the state matches the rows. The recount on open is a check: a difference (which only a defect can cause) is corrected in the row and logged at warn.
errorCases.userImpact: None beyond the failed write itself; completeness never reports counts the store does not hold.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon stops or crashes in the middle of a full index, after the repository's rows were deleted and before the rebuild ended.
errorCases.detection: On the next open the persisted IndexState row has fullIndexFinished false.
errorCases.response: The repository reads not complete ('the full index has not finished'); the daemon's start-up queues a full index for every repository whose fullIndexFinished is false.
errorCases.userImpact: Answers about the repository are marked not established until the queued index ends; nothing is presented as complete.

errorCases.scenario: The V4->V5 migration fails on open (store error while opening the new sub-DBs or writing the IndexState rows).
errorCases.detection: The migration's run() throws inside the migration transaction in getGraphStore.
errorCases.response: The transaction rolls back and the stored schema version stays 4; the open fails with the migration's named error as every other migration step does, and the daemon logs it. No partly migrated store is left.
errorCases.userImpact: The daemon does not start until the cause is fixed; the store is unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: Returning cross-repository incoming relationships to pending fails before the repository's rows are deleted in a reindex.
errorCases.detection: deleteEntitiesForRepo with returnIncomingToPending throws from its write transaction.
errorCases.response: The transaction rolls back, so neither the pending rows nor the delete are applied; the full index fails with status 'error' as today, and the repository keeps its previous rows.
errorCases.userImpact: The reindex is reported failed; the other repository's relationships are not lost.

invariantsToPreserve.text: RepoStatus keeps exactly its four values ('pending' | 'indexing' | 'ready' | 'error'); completeness is an added field beside it, so every consumer that branches on status is unaffected.
A change to what is stored comes with a migration step applied when the daemon opens the store; SCHEMA_VERSION advances 4 -> 5 and the V1->V2, V2->V3 and V3->V4 steps are unchanged.
Existing relation kind bytes are never renumbered: EXPORTS is written with its existing byte 7 and no new byte is added in this Story.
A resolved relationship whose target is not stored yet is never silently dropped; it is kept until its target exists or it is counted.
A reindex is the one command: it deletes the repository's rows in the graph store and the vector store and indexes every file from scratch; there is no separate repair.
Only the daemon opens the stores; IndexState is read and written inside the daemon and reaches the CLI and the plugins through its status and stats requests.
runCrossFileResolver keeps its signature shape and its existing Pass 1 (module-stub rewiring) and Pass 2 behaviour for the kinds it handles today; new options and results are additions.
Entity ids stay deterministic (SHA256 of repo, file, kind and name), so pending rows awaiting an id are completed by the same id after a rebuild.
A stored edge's value stays empty in this Story: the re-export's exported name lives in export_names, not in the edge value, which Story s7 owns for evidence.
graphCompleteness keeps its existing parameters (returned, found, limited, skipped, partlyRead, rule) for its existing callers; only repoCompleteness is added.

Existing edges, pending rows and kind bytes are read unchanged; EXPORTS uses its existing byte 7 with today's empty edge value. The store migration is forward-only: a store at version 5 opened by a daemon built before this change is refused by today's version check (LmdbStoreSchemaVersionMismatch, src/db/graph/store.ts:611-613) rather than read wrongly, so a rollback of the code means restoring the earlier build together with a reindex of a fresh store. Callers of the lookups that read relationships see a completeness of notEstablished, with reasons, where they saw an unqualified result before; the result fields themselves are unchanged. runCrossFileResolver's new mode defaults to 'repository', which matches today's whole-repository behaviour for any caller that does not pass it. updateUnresolvedMeta and updateUnresolvedMetaBatch keep their signatures but now merge meta; their one caller, Pass 2 (src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:343), already passes `{ ...row.meta, candidates }`, so the merge gives it the same row, and a reclass that sets a class other than 'ambiguous' clears a stale candidates list. removeRepo additionally deletes the repository's index_state row.

alternativesConsidered.name: Pending-by-id rows completed by the cross-file pass, IndexState in its own table with transactional counts, re-exports as EXPORTS edges plus an export-name index
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A resolved relationship whose target is not stored becomes a pending row that awaits the target's id, found through a new by-target index and completed by the cross-file pass, across repositories after a reindex; IndexState is a separate per-repository row whose counts are written in the same transactions as the rows they count; a re-export line is stored as an EXPORTS edge plus an entry in an export-name index that the call matcher reads.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Absent target: in upsertResolvedRelations, promoteToResolved and promoteResolvedBatch (called by the cross-file pass and both endpoint passes), a relationship whose target id is not stored (and whose source is) is written as a pending row of the same kind with rawTo = the target id and meta {awaitsId: true, class: 'awaiting-target', file, repo}, keyed makeUnresolvedRelationId(repo, from, kind, awaitedId); when a promotion keeps a row awaiting, the old row is deleted and the re-keyed row written in the same transaction with its by-file and by-target entries and the count change, so one relationship is always one row; a missing source entity, a kind with no byte, a pending row with no file or repository, or a repository that is not registered is counted as unwritable with its reason and logged at warn. The repository a resolved relationship is counted against is its meta.repo; the indexer's resolved writes (the per-file resolver, the manifest step's DEPENDS_ON, the cross-file Pass 1 import rewire, the passes) all carry meta.repo, and a relationship that still names no repository is counted in a daemon-wide unattributed counter returned by daemon.status. A new dupsort sub-DB unresolved_by_target (awaited id -> pending row id), added by a migration step, finds the rows that await a given id in any repository. The cross-file pass runs in one of three explicit modes: 'full' (from fullIndex), 'settle' (from runSettlePass, given the settled files as committedFiles in one call) and 'repository' (from resolveAfterReconcile and any other caller). Its Pass 0 promotes rows whose awaited target now exists: in 'repository' mode, the repository's own awaiting rows; after a settle, the rows awaiting an entity of the committed files; after a full index of repository B, the rows awaiting ANY entity of B, read through unresolved_by_target whichever repository holds them, so the relationships returned to pending by B's reindex are restored in B's own pass and each promoted row's counts are moved in its owning repository's state. Classification: every pending row carries meta.class when written or attempted: rows awaiting an id are 'awaiting-target'; a relative import that resolves to no file is written 'no-candidate' (reason 'target-file-missing') by the per-file resolver; a row awaiting a FILE id whose file exists but is not stored is classed by the full index's own file-selection rule (index.ts:630-640: the repository's ignore list, a parser for the extension, not generated or minified) plus the artifact parser's skip rules (SKIP_BASENAMES and MAX_SIZE, artifact.ts:89, :117-118), extracted so the full index and the cross-file pass apply one rule: a file outside the graph by design (no parser, generated or minified, a lock file, over the size limit) is 'no-candidate' (reason 'target-not-code') and does not block completeness, while a file a parser handles that the ignore rule excludes stays 'awaiting-target' (reason 'target-excluded-by-ignore'), because the graph is really missing it; the cross-file pass writes 'ambiguous' (with candidates) or 'no-candidate' on the rows it attempts; boundary-kind rows are 'external-endpoint'; a row with no class and no awaitsId that the pass has not attempted counts under its kind's default: code-symbol kinds the pass attempts read 'awaiting-target' only until the full index's pass has run, after which unattempted rows are attempted. IndexState: a new sub-DB index_state keyed by repoId holding {generation, pending counts by class, unwritable count, reasonCounts (unwritable and awaiting rows by reason), uncommittedFiles, fullIndexFinished, endpointPassFailed, unembedded, embeddingAvailable}; every write that adds, removes or reclasses a pending row, or counts an unwritable, updates the row in the SAME LMDB write transaction, so an aborted transaction leaves both unchanged; on open the pending counts are recounted from the stored classes and the row corrected if it differs (logged), the rest persisted. RepoCompleteness is derived from it and returned beside the unchanged status by repo.list, repo.stats and daemon.status, shown in the CLI's Repos pane, the JetBrains status dialog and a new VS Code repositories list. Re-exports: the TypeScript parser emits, for `export { a, b as c } from './y.js'`, pending EXPORTS rows from the re-exporting file entity with rawTo = the local name in the source file and meta {specifier, exportedAs}, and for `export * from './y.js'` one row with rawTo '*'. The cross-file pass resolves each to the named entity in the resolved file (or to that file entity for '*'), stores an EXPORTS edge (the existing, unused kind, byte 7, with today's empty value, which Story s7 owns) and, in the same transaction, an entry in a new sub-DB export_names keyed (re-exporting file id, exported name) -> target entity id ('*' entries keyed by the name '*' -> the source file id). resolveCall widens a caller file's candidates: for each imported file it looks up the call's raw name in export_names (and follows '*' entries to their source files), transitively with a visited set, so `export { f as g }` makes g() resolve to f. Reindex: no indexed relationship kind crosses workspace repositories today (Pass 2 is single-repository), so the following is a guard the HLD requires for any that does, such as a hand-written or future cross-repository edge: every full job first writes every relationship that another repository holds into the repository's entities back as a pending row of the holding repository awaiting the entity's id, then deletes the repository's rows in both stores (deleteEntitiesForRepo, deleteUnresolvedForRepo, export_names entries, its IndexState counters) and builds from every file. The repository entity is stored in the full index so the manifest's DEPENDS_ON edges are written. The analyzer's runner context carries the repository's completeness, and graphCompleteness (its existing parameter {returned, found?, limited?, skipped?, partlyRead?, rule?}) gains only repoCompleteness?, so lookups that read relationships mark completeness as not established with the counts when the repository is not complete.
pros: Each piece is one of the HLD's named mechanisms (pending rows completed by their owning pass, one state row, migration steps only) with no change to an existing key or kind byte.
A pending row awaiting an id is found by one index lookup, so the settle pass stays proportional to the committed files.
EXPORTS edges make re-exports visible to every graph reader (import.graph, closures), and export_names keeps the exported name, including an alias, without using the edge value that Story s7 owns.
Counts written in the same transaction as the rows they count cannot drift on an aborted write; the recount on open is a check, not the source.
Pass 0 reading by awaited id across repositories restores another repository's relationships in the reindexed repository's own pass, without reindexing the other repository.
cons: Adds two index sub-DBs (unresolved_by_target, export_names) whose upkeep sits in every pending write, promotion and delete.

Every write that touches a pending row also writes the repository's index_state row, so concurrent counts serialise on that row (LMDB has one writer, so no new contention, but each transaction is larger).
The call matcher's transitive walk through export_names adds reads per call row; bounded by the visited set.
Three new sub-DBs (unresolved_by_target, export_names, index_state) and their migration steps.
The cross-repository return-to-pending guards edges the indexer does not write today, so it is exercised only by a hand-written test fixture until a cross-repository kind exists.

IndexStateRow.description: One row per workspace repository in the new index_state sub-DB, keyed by repoId.

generation.description: Advanced by every write of the repository's rows and every completion.

reasonCounts.description: Count per reason (source-missing, unknown-kind, pending-without-file, repository-not-registered).

uncommittedFiles.description: Paths of files whose parse or write failed in the last full index.

fullIndexFinished.description: The full pass, the cross-file pass and both endpoint passes have ended.

endpointPassFailed.description: Either endpoint pass threw in the last full index.

pending.description: Pending rows by class (awaiting-target, ambiguous, no-candidate, external-endpoint), written in the same transaction as the rows; recounted on open as a check.

rawTo.description: Raw name, specifier, or the awaited entity id when meta.awaitsId is true.

metaAwaitsId.description: meta.awaitsId: rawTo is an entity id.

UnresolvedByTarget.description: New dupsort index from an awaited entity id to the pending rows awaiting it.

ExportName.description: New export_names index: one entry per name a file re-exports, keeping an alias.

exportedName.description: The name the file exports (the alias for `f as g`), or '*'.

targetId.description: The entity re-exported, or the source file for '*'.
